description: THE AUTHORISATION FILTER'S FIRST CONJUNCT, ISOLATED - an administrator is never refused, however the authorisation column reads. This is the controlled comparison to case11: the option, the stub table, the AID, the pinned clock and every other inbound byte are identical, and CDEMO-USER-TYPE alone differs, so exactly one byte of input separates a painted refusal from a transfer. Read the filter cases as one set, because no single fixture can carry everything those eight lines do: case06, case08 and case09 drive the ungated subscript below the valued span, inside the declared table but unvalued, and far beyond it at 99, and between them prove the read is bounded; case10 makes BOTH the validation IF and the filter IF fire in one pass and proves the filter is neither gated by the error flag nor an ELSE of the guard above it; case11 reaches the filter clean with a regular user and is refused by it; and this case is the only arrangement that isolates the FIRST conjunct, because it holds the second conjunct TRUE - the column really is 'A' - while making the first false. The path, statement by statement. app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:77 SET ERR-FLG-OFF TO TRUE and :79-80 MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO establish the preconditions. EIBCALEN is 160, so :82 takes its ELSE and :86 MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) TO CARDDEMO-COMMAREA copies the sixteen-field commarea in. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1, so 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:31 holds, the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :87 is false, and :88-90 - the SET, the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COMEN1AO and the cold paint - all belong to the branch not taken; this is the REENTER side of gate G38, the ENTER side being case02. :92 performs RECEIVE-MENU-SCREEN and the EVALUATE EIBAID at :93 takes its WHEN DFHENTER arm at :94-95 into PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, leaving the WHEN DFHPF3 arm at :96-98 and the WHEN OTHER arm at :99-102 unvisited. Normalising the option. The descending test-before scan at :117-121 examines OPTIONI OF COMEN1AI(WS-IDX:1) from LENGTH OF OPTIONI downwards, finds the '1' of '01' already non-blank at byte 2 and stops with WS-IDX = 2. The two-byte move at :122 fills WS-OPTION-X PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at :45 with '01', so the JUST RIGHT clause has nothing to shift, and the INSPECT WS-OPTION-X REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' at :123 is a no-op because there is no space to replace. :124 leaves WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) at :46 holding 1 and :125 echoes it into OPTIONO, which is why the echoed field would read '01' on any path that painted. The validation guard does not fire. :127-129 is evaluated in source order, gate G30, and all three terms are false: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC is false because '01' is numeric; WS-OPTION > CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT is false because 1 does not exceed this table's active count of 1; and WS-OPTION = ZEROS is false because the option is 1. So :130-133 never run, no 'Please enter a valid option number...' is composed, and WS-ERR-FLG still holds the 'N' of :77. That clean precondition is shared with case11 and is what makes the comparison controlled. Why the table is a stub, and what the stub varies. app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:21 declares CDEMO-MENU-OPT-COUNT PIC 9(02) VALUE 10, and all ten valued CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE columns are 'U' (:29, :35, :41, :47, :53, :59, :65, :72, :78, :84), so the filter's second conjunct is FALSE for every subscript the shipped data can offer and holding it true requires a stub. The table used here is the copybook's own first entry - CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM 1, CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME 'Account View' and CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME 'COACTVWC' from :25-28 - with its authorisation column alone changed to 'A', offered as the only active option. The column is the single variable, which is what keeps this fixture an assertion about the code rather than about the shipped data, and it is the same table case11 uses. The substance. :136-137 is IF CDEMO-USRTYP-USER AND CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE(WS-OPTION) = 'A'. The first conjunct, 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-USER at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:28 VALUE 'U', is FALSE because the commarea supplies CDEMO-USER-TYPE 'A', which satisfies 88 CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN at :27 instead. The conjunction is therefore false and :138-142 - the SET ERR-FLG-ON, the MOVE SPACES, the thirty-three-character 'No access - Admin Only option... ' literal and the paint - are all skipped, even though the column at subscript 1 really does hold 'A'. That is the whole point: the second conjunct is true and the refusal still does not happen, so the refusal case11 observes can only have come from the first conjunct. A translation testing 'not admin' rather than 'is user' would agree with this fixture and disagree with case17, whose user type satisfies neither 88. The dispatch, and every field it moves. :145's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is TRUE, so the block the other filter cases suppress runs here. :146 tests CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)(1:5) NOT = 'DUMMY' and 'COACTVWC' is not a DUMMY entry, so the transfer is taken: :147 MOVE WS-TRANID TO CDEMO-FROM-TRANID writes the 'CM00' of :37 and :148 MOVE WS-PGMNAME TO CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM writes the 'COMEN01C' of :36, both overwriting the inbound 'CC00' and 'COSGN00C' that case11 keeps; :151 MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT resets the context to 0 so the successor sees a first entry; and :152-155 is EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), naming 'COACTVWC' and carrying the commarea. That the commarea travels is asserted rather than assumed, because the transfer at :175-177 does not carry one. What the XCTL makes unreachable. An EXEC CICS XCTL transfers control and does not return, so :157-164 - MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE, MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC, the coming-soon STRING at :159-163 and the PERFORM SEND-MENU-SCREEN at :164 - cannot execute on this path, and neither can the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :107-110. That is why the expectation declares NO send at all, why the termination is XCTL rather than RETURN_TRANSID, why the eighty-byte WS-MESSAGE is still the spaces of :79 rather than any composed text, and why no ERRMSGC colour is stated: nothing is painted, so there is no attribute to pin. Geometry a reviewer can confirm by eye, and the defect it exposes. Each table entry is CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NUM PIC 9(02) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-NAME PIC X(35) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME PIC X(08) plus CDEMO-MENU-OPT-USRTYPE PIC X(01) at app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy:89-92, so 2 + 35 + 8 + 1 = 46 bytes. Ten entries carry VALUE clauses at :25-84, 10 x 46 = 460 bytes, while CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS REDEFINES CDEMO-MENU-OPTIONS-DATA at :87 spans CDEMO-MENU-OPT OCCURS 12 TIMES at :88, 12 x 46 = 552 bytes - so the redefinition is 92 bytes LARGER than the item it redefines and slots 11 and 12 have no backing literal at all. Three nested ranges follow and the filter is unguarded across all of them: what the program calls valid is 1 to 10 (:21), what it declares is 1 to 12 (:88), and what a WS-OPTION PIC 9(02) subscript at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:46 can hold is 0 to 99. Because COBOL subscripts are 1-based and Java indices are 0-based, gate G33, subscript 1 must address the FIRST entry - the one this stub gives the 'A' column - so a translation reading index 1 of a 0-based table would find an unvalued slot, the second conjunct would go false for the wrong reason, and this fixture's isolation of the first conjunct would quietly become vacuous. Defects preserved rather than repaired. The oversized REDEFINES stays oversized. The filter at :136-137 stays unguarded by any error-flag test of its own. The subscript read stays BOUNDED - admin.MainMenuService.isAdminOnlyOption is contractually non-throwing and consults MainMenuOptionTable.optionWithinTable - so that no Java exception appears where COBOL without SSRANGE would have computed an offset and read stray bytes; bounding is faithful, whereas clamping, wrapping, guarding or raising would each be a behaviour change. The 99 ceiling that proves the bound holds at the extreme is case09's subject rather than this one's, and slots 11 and 12 stay dead. Widths, channels and what is deliberately absent. Payload names and widths come from the xxxI and xxxO items only: OPTIONI is PIC X(2) at app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY:132, while OPTIONL COMP PIC S9(4) at :127, OPTIONF at :128 and OPTIONA at :130 are length, flag and attribute metadata and are never payload members. The message is pinned at the eighty bytes of WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl:38 and deliberately NOT at the seventy-eight of ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at COMEN01.CPY:260: the truncating MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :187 loses the last two bytes and is case16's subject, and manufacturing a seventy-eight-byte field here would assert this fixture's own arithmetic instead of the program's. Every value is written out to its full declared width in US-ASCII rather than trimmed, because a trimmed expectation cannot tell a padded field from a short one, and the message is written as eighty spaces for exactly that reason. nextMapset and nextMap are absent rather than blank, because a transfer names no map and a spaces-only map name is refused. Statelessness, security and determinism. Every scrap of conversation state arrives in the request - EIBCALEN 160, the DFHENTER AID byte reproduced by common.CicsAid because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository, risk R-D, the sixteen-field CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the received OPTIONI - and leaves in the response's navigation image; nothing is held server-side, which is gate G37. The unit kind is SERVICE, so admin.MainMenuService is constructed and called as a plain object with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path, which is gate G51. The administrator type is trusted exactly as the source trusts it: :149-150, MOVE WS-USER-ID TO CDEMO-USER-ID and MOVE SEC-USR-TYPE TO CDEMO-USER-TYPE, are COMMENTED OUT and are the program's only mention of any SEC-USER-DATA field, so no USRSEC read re-verifies that this caller really is an administrator, nothing is hashed, and the single PIC X(01) comparison at :137 is the entire authorisation mechanism. This fixture pins that posture rather than improving it - one commarea byte of 'A' is sufficient to bypass the filter entirely - and the bounded read is emphatically not treated as a security control. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:33, the instant every case in this directory pins, and the code page is named US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default. Honestly about that clock: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :212-231 does not run on this path at all, because SEND-MENU-SCREEN performs it at :184 and nothing here paints, so CURDATE and CURTIME are never composed and the pinned instant buys determinism across the directory rather than an assertion here. No colour and no highlight, which is easy to misread. COMEN01C contains no MOVE DFHRED anywhere in its 282 lines and copies no CSSETATY, so the DFHRED-plus-asterisk field highlight COACTUPC applies to an offending input has no counterpart in this program: no xxxA attribute item is ever written, no asterisk appears in any expected value, and gate G38 is honoured through the ENTER-versus-REENTER split rather than through any highlight. This case paints nothing at all, so unlike case11 - which pins ERRMSGC at the map's DECLARED red from app/bms/COMEN01.bms - it states no attribute whatsoever. The only colour this program ever moves is DFHGREEN at :158, on the coming-soon path alone. Provenance, honestly. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COMEN01C.cbl, app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COMEN01.CPY, app/bms/COMEN01.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:399-400, which defines TRANSACTION(CM00) PROGRAM(COMEN01C). None of it was captured from a live COBOL execution: no z/OS or CICS runtime exists in this environment, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, refuses a PROCEDURE DIVISION USING under -x, fails to parse app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy and offers no Language Environment CEE services - eight verified blockers in all, recorded as risk R-A. A statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one could not, so the limits are stated rather than glossed. What this case proves, and what it does not. It decisively proves: the conjunction at :136-137 short-circuits on its first term, so an administrator is never refused however the column reads; the second conjunct is genuinely true here, which is what makes the isolation real rather than vacuous; the error flag stays off; the dispatch at :146-155 runs and names 'COACTVWC' with the commarea; :147, :148 and :151 all move, so CDEMO-FROM-TRANID becomes 'CM00', CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM becomes 'COMEN01C' and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT becomes 0; no screen is painted; and the run reports RETURN-CODE 0, the only value any of this program's terminations can produce, since COMEN01C has no CALL 'CEE3ABD', no ABEND and no RETURN-CODE of its own. What it does NOT prove: that the refusal literal and the flag are right, which is case11; that the bound holds at an extreme subscript, which is case09 at 99 and case08 at 11; that the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO narrowing is right, which is case16; and that the coming-soon composition is right, which needs a DUMMY-prefixed entry. One coincidence is recorded rather than left to be discovered later: because a transfer paints nothing, this case's observable image is identical to case03's, which reaches the same XCTL with the shipped table and a false SECOND conjunct. The two are not redundant - case03 fails the second conjunct where this one short-circuits the first, and the runner asserts isAdminOnlyOption true here and false there - but the fixtures cannot express that difference, because the option table is supplied by the runner and no member of this model carries it. Gates pinned: G15, G18, G30, G33, G37, G38 on its REENTER side, and G51.
